learning: Hypothesis: moving the array to y = 0.065 m removes the remaining line loss, and max_error then falls below 0.06. If line loss is 0 and max_error stays at or above 0.06, turning authority (wheel_track) is the binding limit. If steering_oscillation rises sharply, the forward array is reducing kd's damping.
notes: Keeps the Builder's y = 0.065 m array and the iteration-2 controller unchanged, so the race isolates the array move. Watch line_loss_events and max_error on the oval, where line loss was worst.
rationale: The Builder's geometry moves the 50 mm five-sensor array forward to y = 0.065 m. Iteration 2 (array at y = 0.055 m, same controller) cut line loss on the s-bend and slalom to 1.0 event and kept it at 2.0 on the oval. Max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.069, so the robot still crosses the 0.06 m limit. Progress rose to 0.22, 0.15 and 0.11, and no run finished, so the failure is early loss of control, not speed. Iteration 2 showed steering_oscillation of 0.14 to 0.21, which is low, so there is no jitter problem to fix. I keep the controller identical to iteration 2 (base_speed 1.4, kp 4.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.3, last_direction, same weights). This makes the geometry change the only variable, so the race result can be attributed to the array move. The forward array gives more reaction distance, and the kd term already damps the signal. I do not raise base_speed, since no run has finished and speed margin is unproven. I expect line_loss_events to fall to 0 or near 0 and max_error to ease toward 0.06. If line loss clears but max_error stays at or above 0.06, the next lever is turning authority (narrower wheel_track), which the Builder can propose next iteration.
